static_traits.name: Lin Jing
static_traits.family_status: Parents are from Japan; living in Toronto, Canada
static_traits.social_status: Has a few close friends, but relationships with family and friends are tense due to work pressure and lack of time; has not yet fully shared her stress level with friends
static_traits.medical_history: Without significant physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy; past work stress was manageable through self-care
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly coherent logic, tired and negative tone; cooperative with counseling but skeptical about interventions; tending to focus on the negative with self-criticism

basic_info.main_problem: Being a teacher feels very stressful, although I love my students; working long hours gives me insomnia, making it hard to relax outside work.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because work stress significantly affects my daily life and overall well-being.
growth_experiences: Work-related stress persisting since the start of her teaching career: stemming from high work demands and pressure to meet expectations; previously barely manageable through self-care (relaxation and time management), but in recent years intensified into daily, more pronounced persistent worry on workdays and insomnia; has not yet received counseling; no major physical illness.

core_beliefs: I am not competent at teaching work

special_situations.event: A class did not go well; students have not understood the teaching content
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a class has not achieved the anticipated effect, it means I am not suited to be a teacher / not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Overtime lesson preparation and repeated self-criticism; reduces rest and relaxation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not good enough; I am letting my students down; maybe I should not be a teacher

special_situations.event: Weekday tasks piling up; long overtime hours lead to insufficient sleep
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Must complete all tasks and meet all expectations, otherwise it is a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forces extended work hours; compresses socializing and self-care
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never finish; I will mess up

special_situations.event: Facing high-expectation pressure from school and parents
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only meeting others' expectations proves I am valuable and competent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Spends more time on work and reduces time with friends to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I do not do enough; I will disappoint them

special_situations.event: Reflecting on the day's work after a busy workday
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Any mistake means the whole is not good; the positive side does not matter
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ruminates on problems, makes more task lists in an attempt to fix them
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Today is all problems, I did terribly

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as a competent and valuable teacher who can take good care of students
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure, fearing disappointing students and others, fearing being judged as incompetent
defense_goal: Avoids failure and criticism through overtime and self-harshness
Reducing socializing to lower the risk of being judged and maintain safety

object_relations.object_representation: Harsh and demanding judges (school / parents / ideal self)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes reality testing or restructuring negative thoughts
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting the counselor's suggestions as questioning her ability, thinking 'these methods will not work for me'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Speaking hesitantly, repeatedly emphasizing that previous methods did not work, listing many objective reasons for being unable to change, to maintain existing views.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites her to deeply feel and express emotions (e.g. anxiety, guilt)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Treats emotional expression as something that will lose control or affect work, so tries to separate emotions from events and avoid emotional experience
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Flat narration centered on facts and tasks, reducing emotional vocabulary and subjective feelings, quickly turning the topic back to work details and arrangements.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor affirms one's efforts or abilities, or explores one's strengths
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Hearing others' affirmation as implying higher standards, then criticizing herself 'I am still not enough'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using self-blaming language (e.g. 'I have not done enough''I disappoint my students'), in a guilty tone, lowering self-worth.

manifestations: Relationships with friends and family tense due to work pressure and lack of time
Not yet fully sharing her stress level with close friends
Bound by work demands and the pressure to meet expectations, feeling that teaching occupies one's whole life
Finds it hard to choose rest and self-care, keeps working overtime

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-blame, thinking herself 'not good enough''will mess up'
High worry about failure, ruminating daily
Demands high standards of oneself, facing work and interpersonal matters cautiously and tensely

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Regarding the school's/parents' expectations as personal standards that must be met
Judging self-worth by meeting others' expectations
Sacrifices rest and socializing to meet expectations

contact_model.definition: The individual's boundaries between self and others or groups are unclear, with a tendency toward sameness, dissolving individual awareness, corresponding to 'withdrawal'.
manifestations: Unclear boundaries between self and work, feeling work 'has taken over her whole life'
Finding it hard to say 'no', lacking self-care and personal time

positive_force: Proactively tries various relaxation and time management strategies
Has a few close friends as potential support
Willing to seek counseling and explore thinking patterns
negative_force: Long-term worry and cognitive biases (mental filtering, negating the positive, catastrophic prediction)
Long-term overtime and insufficient sleep lead to physical and mental exhaustion
Social avoidance and relationship tension, insufficient use of support
Builds self-worth excessively on external evaluation

target_behavior.behavior: Work-related persistent anxiety and excessive worry
antecedent: When things do not go as planned
Facing pressure to meet external expectations
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive biases from a long-term high-demand work environment and catastrophic prediction of failure, mental filtering and negating the positive
target_behavior.function: Staying vigilant to avoid being seen as incompetent (providing a short-term sense of control)
target_behavior.consequence: Hard to relax outside work, impaired sleep, decreased work focus

target_behavior.core_reason: Persistent worry about work and failure leads to physiological and cognitive activation, making it hard to fall asleep
target_behavior.function: The vigilance maintained by worry brings a short-term sense of 'readiness' (without intended function)
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased attention,Work performance affected,Physical and mental exhaustion

target_behavior.behavior: Irritability and alienation toward family and friends
antecedent: When stress is high and sleep insufficient
When being questioned or needing to socialize
target_behavior.core_reason: Emotional exhaustion and inner self-blame under high pressure lead to venting emotions on family and friends and avoiding interaction
target_behavior.function: Escapes social needs; saves time and energy to cope with work
target_behavior.consequence: Tense relationships with family and friends, reduced social support
